import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 10
    n_vehicles = 3
    Q = 88  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[87, 47], [95, 60], [70, 27], [91, 30], [28, 18], [84, 91], [44, 25], [50, 7], [83, 62], [25, 38]]
    demands = [25, 6, 20, 25, 24, 19, 14, 24, 14, 5]
    time_windows = [[0, 341], [32, 105], [62, 140], [30, 114], [41, 133], [52, 128], [74, 173], [38, 138], [47, 145], [41, 135], [44, 117]]
    service_times = [9, 15, 12, 13, 6, 7, 8, 15, 12, 13]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

Subject: Vehicle Routing and Scheduling Challenge for the Upcoming Delivery Cycle

Context
We operate a fleet of identical delivery vehicles out of a central depot to serve a set of customers distributed across our service area. The delivery day is governed by a fixed planning horizon, beginning at time 0 and ending when the depot closes. Our objective is to coordinate vehicle routes and schedules so that all customer orders are delivered on time, within capacity, and at the lowest feasible cost.

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
- All vehicles depart the depot at time 0. Each vehicle performs a single continuous trip: it leaves the depot, visits an ordered sequence of customers, and returns to the depot before the depot’s closing time.
- Every customer must be visited exactly once. No split deliveries are allowed.
- Each customer has a delivery time window. The start of service at the customer site must occur within the specified window. If a driver arrives early, the vehicle must wait until the window opens.
- Each stop requires an on-site unloading/service duration. After service is completed, the vehicle departs immediately.
- Travel time between any two locations is based on the straight-line distance between their map coordinates. For planning purposes, one unit of distance equals one unit of time.

Capacity and Service Requirements
- All vehicles are identical in capacity. The total quantity assigned to a vehicle’s route must not exceed its capacity at any point along the trip.
- Customer demand, time window constraints, and service times must all be respected simultaneously when sequencing stops and determining departure and arrival times.

Cost Considerations
- Deploying a vehicle incurs a fixed cost in addition to distance-based travel cost. We will route only as many vehicles as are necessary to meet all customer commitments within the constraints, balancing route length against the fixed cost of placing another vehicle on the road.

Goal
Design a set of feasible routes and visit sequences that:
- Cover every customer exactly once and return all vehicles to the depot before closing,
- Satisfy all time windows (with waiting when arriving early) and service times,
- Respect vehicle capacity limits across each route,
- Minimize the sum of total travel distance and fixed costs for the vehicles used.
